html:
The Pitch Lake at La Brea in southwest Trinidad is the largest natural deposit of asphalt in the world. In 1595 the English explorer Walter Raleigh used its pitch to caulk his ships on his search for El Dorado.

From the late 1800s its asphalt was dug and shipped abroad to pave streets in cities across the United States and Europe. The lake is a sign of the oil below southern Trinidad.

Oil wells followed in the early 1900s, and oil and later natural gas became the country's main wealth, making it one of the richest states in the Caribbean. The oilfield workers' strike led by Uriah Butler in 1937 began in this region.
